https://www.eatingwell.com/kiwi-mojito-m.Title: Gut-Healthy Kiwi Mojito Mocktail
https://www.eatingwell.com/kiwi-mojito-m.Description: This playful twist on the classic mojito trades rum for ripe, juicy kiwis, letting their bright flavor take center stage.
Ingredients: 3 ripe medium kiwis (about 10 ounces total), peeled and sliced (1 cup), plus slices for garnish
2 tablespoons lightly packed fresh mint leaves, plus small sprigs for garnish
Instructions: Combine sliced kiwi, 2 tablespoons mint leaves and 1 tablespoon lime juice in a cocktail shaker. Muddle until the kiwi is mashed to a puree consistency, about 1 minute (you should have about ⅔ cup kiwi mixture).
Divide the kiwi mixture between 2 ice-filled rocks glasses. Top each with ½ cup club soda and stir to combine.
Garnish with additional kiwi slices and mint sprigs, if desired. Recipe developed by Jasmine Smith

https://www.eatingwell.com/lemon-drop-en.Title: Lemon Drop Energy Balls
https://www.eatingwell.com/lemon-drop-en.Description: These no-sugar-added lemon drop energy balls are naturally sweetened with Medjool dates and packed with oats, cashews and hemp seeds.
Ingredients: 12 Medjool dates, pitted and chopped (about 5 ounces; 1 cup)
½ cup unsalted dry-roasted whole cashews
¼ cup lemon juice (from 2 medium lemons)
Instructions: Combine 1 cup oats, the chopped dates, ½ cup cashews and ¼ cup hemp seeds in a food processor. Process until finely chopped, about 2 minutes. Scrape down the sides of the bowl.
Add ¼ cup lemon juice, 2 teaspoons lemon zest and 2 teaspoons vanilla. Pulse until the mixture is smooth and holds together, 2 to 3 pulses.
Roll the mixture into 24 balls (about 2 teaspoons each).
Combine ¼ cup coconut and the remaining 1 teaspoon lemon zest in a small bowl. Roll each ball in the coconut mixture until evenly coated.

https://www.eatingwell.com/creamy-carrot.Title: Creamy Carrot Salad Is So Easy to Make
https://www.eatingwell.com/creamy-carrot.Description: Bright, crunchy and creamy, this carrot salad recipe features plump golden raisins and sliced scallions for an easy side dish.
Ingredients: ¼ cup whole-milk plain strained (Greek-style) yogurt
Instructions: Combine ¼ cup yogurt, ¼ cup mayonnaise, 4 teaspoons vinegar, 2 teaspoons honey, 1 teaspoon turmeric, 1 teaspoon cumin, ¼ teaspoon pepper and ¼ teaspoon salt in a medium salad bowl; whisk well. Add 4 cups carrots, ½ cup raisins and ¼ cup scallions; toss until evenly coated. Let the salad stand at room temperature until the flavors meld, about 10 minutes. Recipe developed by Jasmine Smith

https://www.eatingwell.com/carrot-pineap.Title: Carrot-Pineapple Wellness Shots
https://www.eatingwell.com/carrot-pineap.Description: These ginger, turmeric, carrot and pineapple shots are packed with anti-inflammatory ingredients and make the ideal refreshing drink in the morning.
Ingredients: 1 medium carrot, scrubbed and chopped (about ⅔ cup)
1 tablespoon minced fresh ginger or ½ teaspoon ground ginger
1 teaspoon minced fresh turmeric or ¼ teaspoon ground turmeric
Instructions: Combine 2 cups pineapple, chopped carrot, ⅔ cup water, 1 tablespoon ginger (or ½ teaspoon ground), 1 teaspoon turmeric (or ¼ teaspoon ground), ¼ teaspoon pepper and a pinch of salt in a blender. Process until smooth, about 1 minute.
Strain the mixture through a fine-mesh strainer into a large bowl, pressing lightly on the solids to extract juice. Discard the solids.
Divide between 2 (6-ounce) jars. Cover and refrigerate until chilled, at least 20 minutes or up to 4 days. Recipe developed by Marianne Williams

https://www.eatingwell.com/raspberry-man.Title: This Creamy Raspberry-Mango Chia Seed Smoothie Is Packed with 11 Grams of Fiber
https://www.eatingwell.com/raspberry-man.Description: This creamy smoothie delivers sweet tropical flavors, with frozen mango blending with raspberries and coconut milk for a thick, frosty base.
Ingredients: ½ cup whole-milk plain strained (Greek-style) yogurt
⅓ cup chopped pitted dried dates (about 2 ounces)
Instructions: Combine 1½ cups mango, 1½ cups coconut milk, ½ cup raspberries, ½ cup yogurt, ⅓ cup dates, 1½ tablespoons chia seeds and 1 tablespoon vanilla in a blender; process until smooth and creamy, about 2 minutes.
Divide between 2 (16-ounce) glasses.

https://www.eatingwell.com/sun-dried-tom.Title: Sun-Dried Tomato Vinaigrette
https://www.eatingwell.com/sun-dried-tom.Description: This no-added-sugar vinaigrette uses both sun-dried tomatoes and their flavorful oil, blending with white balsamic, lemon juice and garlic for a zippy dressing.
Ingredients: 3 tablespoons oil from sun-dried tomato jar
⅓ cup finely chopped oil-packed sun-dried tomatoes
Instructions: Combine ⅓ cup sun-dried tomatoes, 3 tablespoons oil from the jar, 3 tablespoons vinegar, 2 teaspoons lemon juice, 1 teaspoon garlic powder, ¼ teaspoon pepper and ¼ teaspoon salt in an 8-ounce container with a tight-fitting lid. Cover and shake vigorously until well combined, about 20 seconds.

https://www.eatingwell.com/protein-oatme.Title: A Bowl of This Oatmeal Delivers 22 Grams of Protein
https://www.eatingwell.com/protein-oatme.Description: This quick and satisfying protein oatmeal recipe features peanut butter and protein powder for staying power while banana slices complete the bowl.
Ingredients: 1 small banana, thinly sliced (about ½ cup)
Instructions: Combine 2¼ cups milk, 1 cup oats, 1 tablespoon brown sugar, 1 teaspoon cinnamon, 1 teaspoon vanilla and ¼ teaspoon salt in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Reduce heat to maintain a gentle simmer; cook, stirring occasionally, until the mixture thickens and most of the liquid is absorbed, about 8 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in 1 tablespoon protein powder.
Divide the oatmeal evenly between 2 bowls. Top each with half the banana slices and 2 teaspoons peanut butter.

https://www.eatingwell.com/clementine-tu.Title: This Clementine-Turmeric Sunshine Shot Can Help Support Immune Health
https://www.eatingwell.com/clementine-tu.Description: Bursting with vitamin C–rich clementines, carrots and fresh turmeric root, this vibrant shot can help support your immune health.
Ingredients: 2 large carrots, peeled and cut into chunks
Instructions: Combine peeled clementines, carrot chunks, ½ cup water and the peeled turmeric in a blender. Process until completely smooth, about 1 minute.
Strain the mixture through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean jar, pressing lightly on the solids to extract the juice. Discard the solids.
Serve immediately or refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Recipe developed by Jasmine Smith

https://www.eatingwell.com/bang-bang-car.Title: Bang Bang Carrots Are an Easy Side You Can Make Tonight
https://www.eatingwell.com/bang-bang-car.Description: These Bang Bang Carrots feature roasted carrots atop a creamy, spicy yogurt sauce for a flavorful side that pairs well with any weeknight meal.
Ingredients: 1 pound medium carrots, scrubbed, halved lengthwise and cut into 2-inch pieces (about 4 cups)
Instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F. Toss carrot pieces with 1 tablespoon oil on a large rimmed baking sheet; spread in an even layer. Roast until tender and lightly browned, flipping once halfway through, 25 to 27 minutes.

Meanwhile, combine 2 tablespoons yogurt, 1 tablespoon mayonnaise, 2¼ teaspoons Sriracha, 1½ teaspoons sweet chili sauce, 1 teaspoon lime juice and ¼ teaspoon onion powder in a medium bowl; whisk until smooth.
Spread the sauce on a large plate. Top with the roasted carrots and sprinkle with 1 teaspoon sesame seeds and 1 tablespoon cilantro.

https://www.eatingwell.com/chickpea-tuna.Title: The Best No-Cook Lunch for the Mediterranean Diet
https://www.eatingwell.com/chickpea-tuna.Description: These Chickpea-Tuna Salad Lettuce Wraps give classic tuna salad a fresh, flavorful upgrade.
Ingredients: 2 (5-ounce) cans no-salt-added tuna in water, drained and flaked
½ cup whole-milk plain strained (Greek-style) yogurt
1 medium stalk celery, thinly sliced (about ⅓ cup)
¼ teaspoon plus ⅛ teaspoon salt
16 butter lettuce leaves (4 ounces; from 1 head)
Instructions: Place rinsed chickpeas in a large bowl. Mash with a fork until some are completely smooth but most remain chunky. Add flaked drained tuna; stir to combine.

Add ½ cup yogurt, 5 tablespoons mayonnaise, the sliced celery, ⅓ cup scallions, ¼ cup capers, 2½ tablespoons lemon juice, 2 tablespoons everything bagel seasoning, ½ teaspoon pepper and ¼ teaspoon plus ⅛ teaspoon salt; mix until evenly combined.
Divide the salad evenly among 16 lettuce leaves (about ¼ cup each), using about 3 to 4 leaves per serving. Recipe developed by Marianne Williams

https://www.eatingwell.com/no-added-suga.Title: No-Added-Sugar Strawberry Protein Shake
https://www.eatingwell.com/no-added-suga.Description: This no-added-sugar high-protein shake recipe blends strawberries, banana, yogurt, dates and a touch of soy milk into a thick, frosty drink.
Instructions: Combine 1 ¼ cups soy milk, 1 cup yogurt and the chopped dates in a blender. Blend until smooth, about 1 minute, starting on low speed and increasing to high.
Add 2 cups frozen strawberries and 2 bananas. Blend until smooth, about 30 seconds. Divide between 2 glasses.

https://www.eatingwell.com/cabbage-salad.Title: Cabbage Salad with Bacon
https://www.eatingwell.com/cabbage-salad.Description: This warm cabbage salad features crisp, smoky bacon while its rendered drippings are whisked into an apple-cider vinaigrette that coats the cabbage.
Ingredients: 1 small head green cabbage (1½ pounds), shredded (about 9 cups)
Instructions: Cook chopped bacon in a large skillet over medium-low heat, stirring often, until crisp, 12 to 14 minutes. Transfer to a large paper towel-lined plate; reserve bacon grease (you should have about 6 tablespoons; add extra-virgin olive oil to reach that amount if needed).
Whisk 6 tablespoons vinegar, 4 teaspoons mustard, 2 teaspoons honey, ½ teaspoon pepper and ⅛ teaspoon salt in a large bowl. Gradually whisk in the reserved bacon grease.
Add shredded cabbage and the drained bacon; toss until evenly coated.

https://www.eatingwell.com/broccoli-sala.Title: 15-Minute Broccoli Salad with Feta
https://www.eatingwell.com/broccoli-sala.Description: Bright, crunchy and ready in just 15 minutes, this broccoli salad features bell peppers, cucumbers and feta tossed in a fresh lemony dressing.
Ingredients: ¼ cup lemon juice (from 1 large lemon)
¼ teaspoon ground pepper, plus more for garnish
¾ cup thinly sliced red onion
2 small Persian cucumbers, sliced into half-moons (about 1¼ cups)
Instructions: Whisk ¼ cup lemon juice, ¼ cup oil, the minced garlic, 1 teaspoon oregano, ¼ teaspoon pepper and ¼ teaspoon salt together in a medium serving bowl until well combined.
Add 5 cups broccoli, 1 cup bell pepper, ¾ cup onion and the sliced cucumbers; toss until evenly coated.
Top with ¼ cup feta. Garnish with additional pepper, if desired.

https://www.eatingwell.com/turmeric-ging.Title: This Turmeric-Ginger Chia Tonic Is Good for Your Gut
https://www.eatingwell.com/turmeric-ging.Description: This tonic is good for your gut health thanks to the fiber in the chia seeds. Fresh orange juice adds brightness, while ginger and turmeric bring warming spice.
Ingredients: 1 medium navel orange, juiced (about ¼ cup)
1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger (from ½-inch piece)
Instructions: In a small microwave-safe bowl, combine orange juice, 1 teaspoon ginger and 1 teaspoon turmeric. Microwave on High until the mixture is gently simmering, 30 to 45 seconds.

Divide the hot mixture evenly between 2 (12-ounce) heatproof glasses (about 2 tablespoons each). Stir 1 cup cold water and 1 tablespoon chia seeds into each glass. Stir until the chia seeds are suspended in the mixture, about 30 seconds.

https://www.eatingwell.com/cheesy-bean-t.Title: Cheesy Bean Toast
https://www.eatingwell.com/cheesy-bean-t.Description: This four-ingredient toast is perfect for using up leftover refried beans. Any salsa works well here, so you can adjust to your spice preferences.
Instructions: Preheat broiler. Place 1 toast slice on a small baking sheet.
Top the toast with ¼ cup warmed refried beans and 1 slice cheese. Broil until the cheese is melted, 1 to 2 minutes. Top with 1 tablespoon salsa.

https://www.eatingwell.com/artichoke-whi.Title: Creamy Artichoke & White Bean Dip Is a High-Protein Appetizer You’ll Love
https://www.eatingwell.com/artichoke-whi.Description: This creamy Artichoke & White Bean Dip brings all the cheesy comfort of a classic baked appetizer, with a plant protein–packed twist!
Ingredients: 1 (10-ounce) jar artichoke hearts in water, rinsed (about 2 cups)
2 (15-ounce) cans no-salt-added cannellini beans, rinsed (about 4 cups)
4 ounces reduced-fat cream cheese, at room temperature
2 teaspoons finely chopped fresh thyme, plus leaves for garnish
¾ cup shredded Gruyère cheese, divided
Multicolored carrots, Belgian endive leaves, Persian cucumbers and/or pita chips, for serving (optional)
Instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F with rack in middle position. Combine rinsed artichoke hearts and 3 garlic cloves in a food processor; process until finely chopped, about 1 minute, scraping down the sides as needed. Transfer to a 12-inch cast-iron or stainless-steel skillet.

Combine rinsed cannellini beans, 1 cup yogurt, 4 ounces cream cheese, ¼ cup Parmesan, 2 teaspoons thyme, 2 teaspoons onion powder and ½ teaspoon pepper in the food processor. Process until smooth, about 2 minutes, scraping down the sides as needed. Add to the skillet with the artichoke mixture; stir to combine. Fold in ¼ cup Gruyère and spread evenly. Top with the remaining ½ cup Gruyère.
Bake until the cheese is melted, about 5 minutes. Increase oven temperature to broil; broil until the cheese is golden brown, about 7 minutes.
Garnish with thyme leaves, if desired. Serve with carrots, endive, cucumbers and/or pita chips, if desired.

https://www.eatingwell.com/white-bean-sk.Title: Easy White Bean Skillet
https://www.eatingwell.com/white-bean-sk.Description: This easy white bean skillet brings together beans, canned tomatoes and fresh greens for a comforting plant-based dinner.
Ingredients: 1 medium yellow onion, finely chopped (about 1½ cups)
3 medium cloves garlic, finely chopped (1 tablespoon)
½ teaspoon salt plus ⅛ teaspoon, divided
¼ teaspoon crushed red pepper, plus more for garnish
1 (28-ounce) can no-salt-added whole peeled tomatoes, undrained and crushed
1 ounce Parmesan cheese, shaved and crumbled (about ⅓ cup)
8 slices whole-wheat baguette (½ ounce each), toasted
Instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add chopped onion; cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 5 minutes. Add 3 tablespoons tomato paste; cook, stirring constantly, until fragrant and deepened in color, 1 to 2 minutes. Stir in chopped garlic, 1½ teaspoons Italian seasoning, ½ teaspoon salt and ¼ teaspoon crushed red pepper; cook, stirring often, until fragrant, about 30 seconds.

Add crushed tomatoes and rinsed beans; bring to a lively simmer over medium heat. Cook, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened, about 3 minutes. Fold in 5 ounces spinach; cook, stirring constantly, until bright green and just wilted, 2 to 3 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in the remaining 2 tablespoons oil. Sprinkle with the remaining ⅛ teaspoon salt.
Divide the mixture among 4 bowls. Sprinkle with crumbled Parmesan. Garnish with additional crushed red pepper, if desired. Serve with toasted baguette slices.

https://www.eatingwell.com/no-added-suga.Title: The Best No-Added-Sugar Smoothie
https://www.eatingwell.com/no-added-suga.Description: This healthy strawberry smoothie is tart and creamy. The frozen strawberries and fresh dates add the perfect amount of sweetness to balance the passion fruit.
Ingredients: ¾ cup frozen passion fruit (6 ounces)
½ cup whole-milk plain strained (Greek-style) yogurt
Instructions: Combine 2 cups almond milk, 2 cups frozen strawberries, ¾ cup frozen passion fruit, ½ cup yogurt, 5 pitted dates, 2 tablespoons chia seeds and 2 teaspoons vanilla in a blender. Process until smooth, about 1 minute.
Divide the smoothie evenly between 2 large glasses and serve.

https://www.eatingwell.com/kale-pineappl.Title: This Kale-Pineapple Drink Is Packed with Potassium to Support Healthy Blood Pressure
https://www.eatingwell.com/kale-pineappl.Description: This refreshing tropical kale-pineapple juice shows just how versatile kale can be. Blanching the greens softens their bitterness and preserves the color.
Ingredients: 2 large curly kale leaves, stemmed and torn into large pieces (about 2 cups)
Instructions: Bring a large saucepan of water to a boil over high heat. Prepare a bowl of ice water; place near the stove. Add torn kale to the boiling water; cook just until vibrant green and tender, 1 to 2 minutes. Using a spider or slotted spoon, transfer the kale to the ice bath. Let stand until cooled, about 2 minutes. Drain well and gently squeeze with your hands to remove excess liquid.
Transfer the blanched kale to a blender. Add 1½ cups pineapple and 1½ cups coconut water. Blend until completely smooth, about 1 minute.
If desired, fill 2 glasses with ice. Pour the juice into the glasses and serve. Recipe developed by Jasmine Smith

https://www.eatingwell.com/high-protein-.Title: This Creamy Orange-Mango Flaxseed Shake Delivers 17 Grams of Protein
https://www.eatingwell.com/high-protein-.Description: Bright, creamy and packed with staying power, this protein shake blends juicy mandarin, tropical mango and tangy strained yogurt into a sunshine-hued drink.
Ingredients: 1 large mandarin or clementine orange (6½ ounces), peeled, plus slices for garnish
Instructions: Combine 1 peeled orange, 1 cup mango, 1¼ cups yogurt, ½ cup ice, ½ cup water, 3 tablespoons ground flaxseed and ½ teaspoon vanilla in a blender. Blend until smooth, about 1 minute.
Divide the shake between 2 tall glasses. Garnish with orange slices, if desired.

https://www.eatingwell.com/raspberry-ban.Title: The Best Gut-Healthy Breakfast
https://www.eatingwell.com/raspberry-ban.Description: This quick and easy breakfast combines creamy Greek-style yogurt with fiber-rich fruit and crunchy toasted pecans for a gut-friendly start to your day.
Ingredients: 1 cup reduced-fat plain strained yogurt, such as Greek-style
Instructions: Spoon ½ cup yogurt into a 16-ounce jar. Top with half the banana slices, ½ cup raspberries and 1 tablespoon pecans. Repeat the layers with the remaining ½ cup yogurt, banana slices, ½ cup raspberries and 1 tablespoon pecans.

https://www.eatingwell.com/no-added-suga.Title: No-Added-Sugar Electrolyte Drink
https://www.eatingwell.com/no-added-suga.Description: This no-sugar-added drink is a simple way to stay hydrated. Electrolyte-rich coconut water is balanced by tart pomegranate juice and a squeeze of fresh lime.
Ingredients: ⅓ cup unsweetened refrigerated pomegranate juice
Instructions: Combine 1½ cups coconut water, ⅓ cup pomegranate juice, 2 tablespoons lime juice and a pinch of salt in a large glass measuring cup; stir until the salt dissolves.
Pour into 2 ice-filled glasses and serve.

https://www.eatingwell.com/chickpea-nood.Title: Chickpea Noodle Soup Is a Cozy, 30-Minute Dinner
https://www.eatingwell.com/chickpea-nood.Description: This cozy Chickpea Noodle Soup is the kind of simple meal that’s worth keeping in your weeknight rotation and features chickpeas, carrots, celery and onion.
Ingredients: 2 medium carrots, peeled and chopped (1 cup)
Instructions: Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a large saucepan over medium-high heat. Add chopped carrots, onion and celery and minced garlic. Cook, stirring often, until the onion is translucent, 3 to 4 minutes.

Stir in 6 cups broth, the rinsed chickpeas, ¾ teaspoon salt and ¼ teaspoon pepper. Bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce heat to maintain a lively simmer; cook until the vegetables begin to soften, 6 to 7 minutes.

Stir in 4 ounces rotini and 1 teaspoon Italian seasoning. Cook, uncovered, stirring occasionally, until the pasta is al dente, 7 to 8 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in 2 tablespoons lemon juice and 1 tablespoon parsley.

https://www.eatingwell.com/focaccia-sand.Title: Focaccia Sandwiches
https://www.eatingwell.com/focaccia-sand.Description: From a tomato-mozzarella version to a fig and goat cheese version, these Italian-inspired focaccia sandwiches are an easy lunch idea.
Ingredients: 1 (8.5-ounce) loaf focaccia, cut into 4 pieces, sliced horizontally and toasted
4 (0.5-ounce) slices cured meat, such as prosciutto, salami or capicola
1 (8.5-ounce) loaf focaccia, cut into 4 pieces, sliced horizontally and toasted
4 (0.5-ounce) slices cured meat, such as prosciutto, salami or capicola
Instructions: To make Tomato, Mozzarella & Pesto Sandwich: Place toasted focaccia slices on a cutting board. Spread 1½ teaspoons pesto on 4 focaccia slices. Top each with 1 slice meat and 1 slice mozzarella. Top evenly with sliced tomatoes. Drizzle each with 1 teaspoon balsamic glaze. Top each with a remaining focaccia slice. Cut in half and serve.

To make Fig & Goat Cheese Sandwich: Place toasted focaccia slices on a cutting board. Divide 3 ounces goat cheese among 4 focaccia slices; spread to cover. Top each with 1½ teaspoons fig jam. Top each with 1 slice meat and ¼ cup arugula. Drizzle each with ½ teaspoon balsamic glaze. Top each with a remaining focaccia slice. Cut in half and serve.

https://www.eatingwell.com/chopped-beet-.Title: This Chopped Salad Is the Best Way to Eat Beets
https://www.eatingwell.com/chopped-beet-.Description: This vibrant Chopped Beet Salad delivers a refreshing balance of earthy, tangy and citrusy flavors in every bite.
Ingredients: ¼ teaspoon plus ⅛ teaspoon salt
3 cups chopped refrigerated cooked beets (three 8.8-ounce packages)
½ cup crumbled feta cheese (2 ounces)
Instructions: Whisk 2 tablespoons oil, 1½ teaspoons orange zest, 2 tablespoons orange juice, 1½ tablespoons vinegar, 1 teaspoon mustard, 1 teaspoon honey, ¼ teaspoon plus ⅛ teaspoon salt and ¼ teaspoon pepper together in a large bowl. Set aside 2 tablespoons of the dressing for drizzling.

Add 3 cups chopped beets to the bowl; toss with the remaining dressing until evenly coated. Transfer to a serving bowl and top with ½ cup crumbled feta and 1½ tablespoons pistachios. Drizzle with the reserved dressing. Garnish with chopped mint, if desired.

https://www.eatingwell.com/crispy-smashe.Title: Crispy Smashed Beets with Feta & Pistachios
https://www.eatingwell.com/crispy-smashe.Description: These crispy smashed beets are a flavorful side dish and are topped with tangy feta, crunchy pistachios and a drizzle of honey.
Ingredients: 2 tablespoons chopped fresh dill or mint
Instructions: Preheat oven to broil with a rack in middle position. Line a large rimmed baking sheet with foil; coat foil with cooking spray.

Slice beets into ½-inch-thick rounds. Pat dry with a paper towel. Transfer the beet rounds to a large bowl; toss with 1 tablespoon cornstarch, ¼ teaspoon pepper and ¼ teaspoon salt until evenly coated. Arrange the beets in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet. Using the bottom of a Mason jar or sturdy glass, press on each beet to flatten it, but keep it intact. Drizzle the beets evenly with 2 tablespoons oil.
Broil until the edges are crispy and browned, 13 to 16 minutes, rotating the pan front to back halfway through.
Transfer the beets to a serving platter. Drizzle with 1 tablespoon honey; top with ¼ cup feta and 2 tablespoons each pistachios and herbs. Serve warm or at room temperature.

https://www.eatingwell.com/20-minute-bla.Title: 20-Minute Black Bean Soup
https://www.eatingwell.com/20-minute-bla.Description: This easy black bean soup takes only 20 minutes from start to finish, making it perfect for busy weeknights when you want something satisfying.
Ingredients: 2 (15-ounce) cans no-salt-added black beans, rinsed (about 3 cups)
1 (10-ounce) package frozen chopped sweet potatoes (about 2 cups), thawed
1 (8-ounce) package cream cheese, cut into pieces, softened
Instructions: Stir 4 cups broth, the rinsed beans, the thawed sweet potatoes, 1 can tomatoes, the chopped onion, 1 cup corn, 1 tablespoon garlic paste, 1 teaspoon taco seasoning, ½ teaspoon salt, ½ teaspoon chipotle and ¼ teaspoon pepper together in a large Dutch oven. Cover and bring to a boil over high heat.
Uncover, reduce heat to medium and cook, undisturbed, until the sweet potatoes are tender, about 10 minutes.

Stir in softened cream cheese. Bring to a lively simmer, uncovered, over medium heat; simmer for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until smooth and the flavors meld. Divide among 6 bowls. Garnish with cilantro, if desired.

https://www.eatingwell.com/marry-me-whit.Title: Marry Me White Bean Soup
https://www.eatingwell.com/marry-me-whit.Description: This Marry Me White Bean Soup borrows inspiration from the beloved Marry Me Chicken recipe with a combination of sun-dried tomatoes, garlic, cream and Parmesan.
Ingredients: 1 medium yellow onion, finely chopped (about 1 cup)
½ cup chopped drained julienne-cut sun-dried tomatoes in oil with herbs
2 (15-ounce) cans no-salt-added white beans (such as great northern or cannellini), rinsed
Instructions: Melt 2 tablespoons butter in a large Dutch oven over medium heat. Add chopped onion; cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 3 minutes. Add chopped garlic, 1 teaspoon oregano, ½ teaspoon salt and ¼ teaspoon crushed red pepper; cook, stirring constantly, until fragrant, about 20 seconds. Add ½ cup chopped sun-dried tomatoes; cook, stirring, until slightly darkened, about 2 minutes. Add 1 tablespoon lemon juice; stir until absorbed, about 20 seconds.

Stir in rinsed beans and 4 cups broth. Bring to a lively simmer over medium-high heat. Stir in ½ cup cream and 2 tablespoons cream cheese; cook, stirring, until the cream cheese is melted, 2 to 3 minutes.
Add 5 ounces spinach; cook, stirring occasionally, until wilted, about 2 minutes. Remove from heat. Add 1 cup Parmesan; stir until melted.
Divide the soup among 6 bowls. Top with ¼ cup basil and the remaining ¼ cup Parmesan.

https://www.eatingwell.com/spinach-artic.Title: Spinach & Artichoke Dip Soup
https://www.eatingwell.com/spinach-artic.Description: This creamy soup captures the essence of spinach-artichoke dip perfectly.
Ingredients: 1 (10-ounce) package frozen spinach, thawed and drained
1 (12-ounce) package frozen artichoke hearts, thawed and coarsely chopped
1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese, plus more for serving
Instructions: Whisk cream cheese and milk together in a medium bowl until smooth, about 2 minutes.

Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add onion; cook, stirring often, until softened and slightly translucent, about 4 minutes. Add garlic; cook, stirring often, until fragrant, about 1 minute. Add spinach; cook, stirring often to break up any clumps, until separated and warmed through, about 3 minutes. Add broth and artichoke hearts; stir to combine. Bring to a boil over medium heat. Cook, undisturbed, until the artichokes and spinach are completely warmed through and the broth is slightly reduced, about 3 minutes; remove from heat.
Working in 3 batches, whisk in the reserved cream cheese mixture until melted and creamy, about 2 minutes. Add Parmesan, lemon juice and salt, stirring until the cheese is melted.
Ladle into 8 bowls. Sprinkle with pepper; serve with additional Parmesan, if desired.

https://www.eatingwell.com/creamy-sun-dr.Title: Creamy Sun-Dried Tomato & Spinach Soup with Ravioli
https://www.eatingwell.com/creamy-sun-dr.Description: This soup is delightfully creamy, flavored with sweet sun-dried tomatoes and cheesy ravioli.
Ingredients: 2 tablespoons oil from sun-dried tomato jar
1/2 cup oil-packed sun-dried tomatoes, coarsely chopped, plus 2 tablespoons oil from the jar
Instructions: Heat sun-dried tomato oil in a large saucepan over medium-high heat. Add sun-dried tomatoes and onion; cook, stirring occasionally, until the onion is translucent, about 3 minutes. Stir in garlic paste, Italian seasoning and crushed red pepper; cook, stirring constantly, until fragrant, about 1 minute.

Stir in broth; bring to a boil over high heat. Add ravioli; cook, stirring occasionally, until al dente, about 5 minutes. Whisk cornstarch and 1 tablespoon water together in a small bowl; drizzle into the boiling soup. Cook, stirring, until slightly thickened, about 1 minute. Remove from heat.
Add spinach, cream and lemon juice; stir until the spinach is wilted, about 1 minute.

https://www.eatingwell.com/white-bean-so.Title: 20-Minute White Bean Soup
https://www.eatingwell.com/white-bean-so.Description: This fiber-rich soup is an easy, healthy dinner when you’re pressed for time. This brothy soup is finished with a bit of heavy cream for body and richness.
Ingredients: 2 cups frozen chopped sweet potatoes, thawed
2 cups frozen chopped collard greens, thawed
Instructions: Combine broth, sweet potatoes, collard greens, beans, onion, celery, lemon juice, garlic, garlic-and-herb seasoning, salt, pepper and crushed red pepper in a large Dutch oven. Bring to a boil over high heat. Cover, reduce heat to medium and cook, undisturbed, until the sweet potatoes are tender, about 10 minutes.
Stir in cream. Bring to a simmer, uncovered, over medium heat; simmer for 5 minutes. Divide among 6 bowls. Top with Parmesan.

https://www.eatingwell.com/creamy-mushro.Title: 20-Minute Creamy Mushroom Soup with Sherry
https://www.eatingwell.com/creamy-mushro.Description: This creamy mushroom soup is loaded with earthy wild mushrooms enhanced by the flavor of dry sherry.
Ingredients: 16 ounces sliced mixed wild mushrooms, such as cremini, oyster and shiitake
1/2 teaspoon ground pepper, plus more for garnish
Instructions: Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add mushrooms; cook, stirring occasionally, until lightly browned, about 6 minutes. Stir in shallots, garlic paste and thyme; cook, stirring often, until the shallots are translucent and the mixture is fragrant, about 2 minutes. Add sherry; cook, stirring to release any browned bits, until mostly absorbed, 1 to 2 minutes.
Reserve 1/3 cup broth in a small measuring cup or bowl. Add the remaining 3 2/3 cups broth, salt and pepper to the pot; bring to a boil over high heat.

Whisk cornstarch into the reserved broth until smooth. Pour the mixture into the boiling soup, whisking to incorporate. Cook, stirring constantly, until thickened, 30 to 45 seconds. Stir in cream and vinegar.

Transfer 1 cup of soup to a blender; blend until smooth, about 45 seconds (use caution when blending hot liquids). Stir the pureed soup back into the pot. Serve hot; garnish with cracked black pepper, if desired.

https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/806839.Title: Creamy Sausage & Cheese Tortellini Soup
https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/806839.Description: This cheese tortellini soup recipe is a quick meal to throw together on a weeknight, and a crowd-pleaser if you have company.
Ingredients: 1 pound mild or hot Italian pork sausage, casings removed
1 (15-ounce) can no-salt-added diced tomatoes with basil, garlic and oregano, undrained
1 (9-ounce) package refrigerated cheese tortellini (such as Buitoni)
Instructions: Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add sausage; cook, stirring to crumble, until browned and no longer pink, about 5 minutes. Add onion and carrot; cook, stirring occasionally, until the onion is translucent, about 4 minutes. Add garlic and Italian seasoning; cook, stirring constantly, until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Stir in broth and tomatoes; bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce heat to medium to maintain a simmer; cook, covered, until the carrots are tender, about 5 minutes.
Uncover and return to a boil over high heat. Add tortellini. Reduce heat to maintain a gentle boil; cook according to package directions.
Reduce heat to medium-low; stir in spinach and half-and-half. Stir gently until the spinach wilts, about 1 minute. Ladle the soup into 6 bowls. Additional reporting by Carrie Myers and Jan Valdez

https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/263772.Title: Spicy Coconut, Chicken & Mushroom Soup
https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/263772.Description: Coconut milk tames the heat and combines deliciously with shredded chicken breast in this spicy Thai-inspired coconut chicken soup.
Ingredients: 2 teaspoons sambal oelek (ground fresh chile paste)
3 cups Chicken stock or reduced-sodium chicken broth
2 cups shredded cooked chicken breast (about 8 ounces)
Instructions: Heat a Dutch oven over medium heat. Add oil to pan; swirl to coat. Add mushrooms, bell pepper, ginger, garlic and lemongrass; cook 3 minutes, stirring occasionally. Add chile paste; cook 1 minute. Add chicken stock, coconut milk, fish sauce and sugar; bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low; simmer for 10 minutes. Add chicken to pan; cook 1 minute or until thoroughly heated. Discard lemongrass. Top with onions, cilantro and juice.

https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/793707.Title: Marry Me Chicken Soup
https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/793707.Description: This creamy soup draws inspiration from "marry me" chicken, a dish that features chicken and sun-dried tomatoes. We add to the soup by including zucchini and carrots to create a cozy, warming meal.
Ingredients: 0.3333 cup slivered oil-packed sun-dried tomatoes, plus 2 tablespoons oil from the jar
Instructions: Heat sun-dried tomato oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add onion and carrots; cook, stirring, until softened, about 4 minutes. Add garlic and Italian seasoning; cook, stirring for 1 minute. Add flour; cook, stirring, for 1 minute more. Add milk, broth, salt and pepper; increase heat to medium-high and bring to a simmer. Add zucchini and sun-dried tomatoes; cook, stirring occasionally and reducing the heat to maintain a simmer, until the zucchini is tender, about 8 minutes. Add spinach and chicken; cook, stirring, until the spinach is wilted and the soup is hot, about 2 minutes more. Remove from heat and stir in vinegar.

https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/275923.Title: Creamy Chicken Noodle Soup with Rotisserie Chicken
https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/275923.Description: This creamy chicken noodle soup recipe has a delicious potpie feel to it. Pair this comforting soup with a green salad or a sandwich.
Ingredients: 2 cups chopped yellow onion (from 1 large onion)
3 cups coarsely chopped rotisserie chicken breast (from 2 rotisserie chickens)
Instructions: Melt 2 tablespoons butter with 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add 2 cups onion, 1 cup carrots, 1 cup celery and 1¾ teaspoons salt and cook, stirring often, until vegetables are slightly softened, 6 to 8 minutes. Add 3 tablespoons flour and stir to coat. Stir in 4 cups stock and 2 cups milk and let the mixture come to a boil. Add 4 ounces uncooked noodles to the boiling mixture. Cover and cook until noodles are al dente, about 8 minutes. Stir in 3 cups chicken and 1 cup peas and cook until pasta reaches desired doneness and chicken and peas are warmed through, about 1 to 2 more minutes. Serve immediately.

https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/795891.Title: Creamy Sun-Dried Tomato & Spinach Soup
https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/795891.Description: Loaded with umamiful tomatoes, creamy beans and bright lemon, this soup could be on your table in 30 minutes.
Ingredients: 0.3333 cup slivered oil-packed sun-dried tomatoes, plus 2 tablespoons oil from the jar
1 (15 ounce) can unsalted cannellini beans, rinsed
1 tablespoon lemon juice, plus more to taste
Instructions: Heat 2 tablespoons sun-dried tomato oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add mushrooms and onion; cook, stirring, until starting to soften, about 3 minutes.
Add garlic and basil; cook, stirring, for 1 minute. Add flour, salt and pepper; cook, stirring, for 1 minute. Add broth and cream; increase heat to medium-high and bring to a simmer.

Reduce heat to maintain a simmer and cook, stirring once or twice, until the vegetables are soft, about 5 minutes. Stir in spinach, beans and sun-dried tomatoes; cook, stirring, until the spinach is wilted, about 2 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in lemon juice.

https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/270499.Title: Immune Supporting Creamy Tomato Soup (Pack It for Lunch!)
https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/270499.Description: This 3-ingredient easy soup recipe is perfect for a satisfying and healthy afternoon snack or a quick lunch.
Instructions: Whisk tomatoes, broth and cream cheese in a large heatproof mug. Microwave on High, stirring occasionally, until heated through and creamy, about 2 minutes.

https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/277432.Title: Cream of Broccoli Soup
https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/277432.Description: This simple and healthy cream of broccoli soup recipe gets its flavor from a mixture of aromatic vegetables, including leeks and celery. Using an immersion blender (or regular blender) gives it a smooth, creamy texture. Enjoy this easy homemade cream of broccoli soup as a comforting appetizer or pair it with a sandwich or salad for lunch or dinner.
Ingredients: 2 medium leeks, white and light green parts only, sliced and rinsed
4 cups low-sodium vegetable broth or low-sodium chicken broth
Instructions: Melt butter in a large saucepan over medium-high heat. Add leeks and celery; cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, 6 to 8 minutes. Add garlic; cook, stirring constantly, until fragrant, about 1 minute.

Add broccoli and broth; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to medium; cover and cook until the broccoli is tender, about 12 minutes. Stir in thyme and salt. Puree the soup with an immersion blender until smooth, about 2 minutes. (Alternatively, transfer soup, in batches if necessary, to a blender. Remove center piece of blender lid to allow steam to escape; secure lid on blender. Place a clean kitchen towel over opening in lid. Process until smooth, about 2 minutes. Use caution when blending hot liquids.) Add half-and-half and process just until incorporated, about 15 seconds. Serve immediately, topped with chives. Recipe developed by Marianne Williams

https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/275929.Title: Healthy Cream of Mushroom Soup
https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/275929.Description: This healthy mushroom soup recipe is rich and creamy with some texture from the mushrooms. Learn how to make this delicious mushroom soup for dinner.
Ingredients: 2.5 pounds cleaned and sliced fresh mixed mushrooms
Instructions: Roughly chop mushrooms. Add oil and butter to a large, heavy pot and cook over medium-high until butter melts. Add mushrooms, salt, and pepper; cook, stirring often, until mushrooms are deeply browned and most of the moisture has evaporated, 8 to 10 minutes.

Add shallots and scallions; cook, stirring often, until softened, about 4 minutes. Add flour and stir to combine. Add stock and milk, stirring and scraping to loosen any browned bits from bottom of pot. Let mixture come to a low boil and cook, stirring occasionally, until broth thickens, about 5 minutes. Remove from heat. Transfer half of mixture to a countertop blender. Secure lid on blender and remove center piece to allow steam to escape. Place a clean towel over opening and process until almost smooth; return to pot. Or use an immersion blender to pulse the soup until somewhat blended but some whole pieces of mushroom are still visible. Stir in parsley and tarragon; serve hot.

https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/250925.Title: Creamy Radish Soup
https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/250925.Description: In this radish soup recipe, radishes are sautéed and pureed with potato, creating a velvety, healthy soup. Learn how to make it today.
Ingredients: 1 medium Yukon Gold potato (about 8 ounces), peeled and cut into 1-inch cubes
1 tablespoon chopped fresh radish greens or parsley
Instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium-high heat. Add 1 3/4 cups radishes and onion and cook, stirring frequently, until the onions are beginning to brown and the radishes are translucent, about 5 minutes. Add potato, milk, salt and pepper to taste. Bring to a boil, stirring occasionally. Reduce heat to a simmer, cover and cook, stirring occasionally, until the potato is tender, about 5 minutes more.
Working in batches, puree the mixture in a blender (or in the pan with an immersion blender) until smooth. (Use caution when pureeing hot liquids.)
Slice the remaining 1/4 cup radishes into matchsticks. Serve each portion of soup topped with 1 tablespoon sour cream, some radish matchsticks and a sprinkling of radish greens (or parsley).

https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/278874.Title: Sheet-Pan Chili-Lime Salmon with Potatoes & Peppers
https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/278874.Description: Busy weeknights beg for something simple like this salmon sheet-pan dinner. Like the name suggests, it's all cooked on one pan. The potatoes get a head start, followed by sweet bell peppers and finally chili-coated salmon fillets. It's a complete meal with easy cleanup!
Ingredients: 1 pound Yukon Gold potatoes, cut into 3/4-inch pieces
2 medium bell peppers, any color, sliced
1.25 pounds center-cut salmon fillet, skinned, if desired, and cut into 4 portions
Instructions: Preheat oven to 425 degrees F. Coat a large rimmed baking sheet with cooking spray.
Toss potatoes, 1 tablespoon oil, 1/4 teaspoon salt and pepper together in a medium bowl. Transfer to the prepared pan and roast for 15 minutes.

Meanwhile, combine chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, lime zest and the remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt in a small bowl. Place bell peppers in the medium bowl and add the remaining 1 tablespoon oil and 1/2 tablespoon of the spice mixture; toss well to coat. Coat the salmon with the remaining spice mixture.

After 15 minutes, remove the pan from the oven. Add the peppers and stir to combine. Roast for 5 minutes. Remove from the oven; move some of the vegetables over and add the salmon to the pan. Roast until the salmon is just cooked through, 6 to 8 minutes. Serve with lime wedges.

https://www.eatingwell.com/bhel-puri-ins.Title: This High-Fiber Salad Is Inspired By Indian Street Food and Helps Me Manage My Blood Sugar
https://www.eatingwell.com/bhel-puri-ins.Description: This flavorful salad was inspired by bhel puri, a type of chaat (savory snack) served across India, and features puffed quinoa and lentils for extra protein and fiber.
Ingredients: 1 small green or red bell pepper, finely diced
1 large English hothouse cucumber or 3 Persian cucumbers, finely diced
1 jalapeno, seeded to taste and finely diced
2/3 cup sweet corn kernels (roasted or cooked if fresh and thawed if frozen)
1/2 cup finely chopped Roma or cherry tomatoes
Instructions: Evenly divide lentils, bell pepper, cucumber, jalapeño (if using), corn and quinoa between two bowls. Drizzle with tamarind-date chutney and coriander chutney. Top with tomatoes, onion, cilantro and peanuts.

https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/278503.Title: Mushroom-Swiss Turkey Burgers
https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/278503.Description: In this gluten-free turkey burger recipe, lean ground turkey stands in for ground beef, and portobello mushrooms produce a juicy, flavorful alternative to the traditional bun. Melted Swiss cheese, sliced tomato and arugula top off this delicious low-carb dinner!
Ingredients: 8 portobello mushroom caps, stems and gills removed (see Tips)
Instructions: Preheat grill to medium-high (400-450 degrees F). Combine oil, garlic and 1/4 teaspoon each pepper and salt in a small bowl. Brush portobello caps with the oil mixture; set aside to marinate at room temperature for 10 minutes.

Meanwhile, combine ground turkey, Worcestershire, mustard and the remaining 1/2 teaspoon pepper and 1/4 teaspoon salt in a medium bowl. Gently mix to incorporate. (Do not overmix.) Shape into four 3/4-inch-thick patties and set aside.

Oil the grill rack (see Tips). Place the mushrooms, cap-side down, on the oiled grill rack. Grill, covered, until just tender, about 4 minutes per side. Transfer the mushrooms to a plate; cover to keep warm. Oil the rack again; place the turkey patties on the oiled rack. Grill, covered, until the patties are lightly charred and an instant-read thermometer inserted in the center registers 165 degrees F, 4 to 5 minutes per side. Place 1 cheese slice on each patty during the last minute of cooking. Transfer the patties to a plate and let rest for 5 minutes. (If your grill is large enough, grill the portobello caps and the patties at the same time.)
Place each patty on the stem side of a portobello cap; top evenly with tomato slices and arugula. Cover with the remaining portobello caps, stem-side down, and serve immediately.

https://www.eatingwell.com/chicken-brocc.Title: Chicken & Broccoli Stir-Fry
https://www.eatingwell.com/chicken-brocc.Description: This juicy chicken and broccoli stir-fry features tender-crisp broccoli coated in a velvety sauce flavored with hoisin—a flavorful sauce made from fermented soybean paste that strikes the perfect balance between sweet and tangy.
Ingredients: 2 (8-ounce) boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut into 1-inch cubes
Instructions: Evenly season chicken with black pepper and salt. Heat 1 tablespoon canola oil in a large nonstick skillet or wok over medium heat. Add the chicken; cook, stirring occasionally, until lightly browned and a thermometer inserted in the thickest parts 165°F, 7 to 8 minutes. Transfer to a plate. Do not wipe the pan clean.

Return the pan to medium heat. Add broccoli and the remaining 1 tablespoon canola oil; stir until the florets are fully coated. Add 1/4 cup water; cover, and cook, undisturbed, until the broccoli is bright green and tender-crisp, about 2 minutes.

Whisk broth, hoisin, soy sauce, sesame oil, ginger, garlic, vinegar and white pepper together in a small bowl until fully combined. Pour the mixture over the broccoli; continue cooking over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until the mixture reduces by one-quarter, about 3 minutes.

Whisk cornstarch and the remaining 1 tablespoon water together in a small bowl. Add to the pan; cook, stirring constantly, until the sauce has slightly thickened and coats the back of a spoon, about 1 minute.

Reduce heat to low. Add the chicken; cook, stirring, until evenly coated and heated through, about 3 minutes. Sprinkle with scallions and sesame seeds. Additional reporting by Carrie Myers, M.S. and Linda Frahm

https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/275786.Title: Smoked Salmon Stuffed Baked Potatoes
https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/275786.Description: Step aside, bacon--these loaded baked potatoes are stuffed with smoked salmon, sour cream and chives for a fresh take on this comfort-food staple, and an easy healthy dinner.
Ingredients: 4 ounces smoked salmon, cut into 1-inch pieces
Instructions: Pierce potatoes all over with a fork. Microwave on Medium, turning once or twice, until soft, about 20 minutes. (Alternatively, bake potatoes at 425 degrees F until tender, 45 minutes to 1 hour.) Transfer to a clean cutting board and let cool slightly.
Holding them with a kitchen towel to protect your hands, make a lengthwise cut to open the potato, but don't cut all the way through. Pinch the ends to expose the flesh.
Top each potato with some sour cream, tomato, onion, salmon and chives. Serve warm.

https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/276964.Title: Baked Halibut with Brussels Sprouts & Quinoa
https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/276964.Description: Fish plus two sides? It seems fancy, but this healthy dinner comes together in just 30 minutes.
Ingredients: 1 pound Brussels sprouts, trimmed and sliced
1 fennel bulb, trimmed and cut into strips
1 tablespoon plus 1 teaspoon olive oil, divided
1 (1 pound) halibut fillet, cut into 4 portions
2 tablespoons chopped fresh Italian parsley or fennel fronds
Instructions: Position racks in upper and lower thirds of oven; preheat to 400 degrees F.

Combine Brussels sprouts, fennel, 1 Tbsp. oil, and 1/4 tsp. each salt and pepper in a large bowl; toss to coat. Spread in a single layer on a large rimmed baking sheet. Bake, stirring occasionally, until tender, 20 to 25 minutes.

Meanwhile, place halibut on another large rimmed baking sheet and top with half of the garlic and the remaining 1/4 tsp. each salt and pepper. Combine lemon juice and melted butter in a small bowl. Drizzle or brush half of the mixture over the fish. Bake until the fish is opaque and flakes easily with a fork, 12 to 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, combine quinoa, the remaining 1 tsp. oil, sun-dried tomatoes, olives, and parsley (or fennel fronds) in a medium bowl.
Add the remaining garlic to the lemon-butter mixture. Pour the mixture over the vegetables and bake for 1 minute more. Serve the halibut and vegetables alongside the quinoa mixture.

https://www.eatingwell.com/eat-the-rainb.Title: Eat-the-Rainbow Vegetable Soup
https://www.eatingwell.com/eat-the-rainb.Description: Tomatoes and carrots are just a few of the veggies that help fight inflammation in this grab-and-go soup.
Instructions: Divide tomato sauce among 3 (1-pint) canning jars (or other microwaveable airtight containers). Top each with 1/2 cup lima beans and 1/3 cup each carrots, bell pepper, tomatoes and spinach. Cover and refrigerate for up to 3 days.

To prepare 1 jar of soup: Add 3/4 cup broth to the jar; sprinkle with 1/4 teaspoon each Italian seasoning, garlic powder and crushed red pepper and a pinch of salt. Microwave, uncovered, on High in 1-minute increments, stirring after each, until the soup is steaming hot and the vegetables are tender, 4 to 5 minutes total. Let cool for 5 minutes before serving. Recipe developed by Jasmine Smith

https://www.eatingwell.com/veggie-fajita.Title: Veggie Fajitas
https://www.eatingwell.com/veggie-fajita.Description: These veggie fajitas are packed with sweet bell pepper and red onion. Creamy avocado and warm tortillas complete the meal.
Ingredients: 4 small multicolored bell peppers, thinly sliced
1/4 cup chopped fresh cilantro, plus cilantro leaves for garnish
Instructions: Heat oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Add bell peppers and onion; cook, stirring occasionally, until tender and slightly charred, about 12 minutes.

Stir in black beans, water, cumin, chili powder, paprika, salt and pepper; cook, stirring often, until the beans are heated through and the spices coat the vegetables, about 4 minutes. Remove from heat; stir in cilantro and lime juice.
Divide the mixture among tortillas; top with cotija and avocado. Garnish with cilantro leaves, if desired. Additional reporting by Carrie Myers, M.S. and Jan Valdez

https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/275787.Title: Cheeseburger Stuffed Baked Potatoes
https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/275787.Description: Skip the bun and serve all of your favorite cheeseburger ingredients--beef, cheese, tomatoes, red onions and lettuce--with baked potatoes for a hearty and easy dinner recipe that kids and adults will love. Feel free to swap out the ground beef for ground turkey or tofu crumbles.
Instructions: Pierce potatoes all over with a fork. Microwave on Medium, turning once or twice, until soft, about 20 minutes. (Alternatively, bake potatoes at 425 degrees F until tender, 45 minutes to 1 hour.) Transfer to a clean cutting board and let cool slightly.
Holding them with a kitchen towel to protect your hands, make a lengthwise cut to open the potato, but don't cut all the way through. Pinch the ends to expose the flesh.
Top each potato with some mayonnaise, beef, lettuce, tomato, red onion and cheese. Serve warm.

https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/275771.Title: Pan-Seared Steak with Crispy Herbs & Escarole
https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/275771.Description: This easy dinner takes just 20 minutes to prepare, meaning that seared steak can be a weeknight meal. Cooking herbs in the pan with the steak releases their aroma, infusing it into the meat while creating a crispy garnish. After the steaks and herbs are pan-seared, the escarole is cooked in the same skillet, so this healthy dinner requires minimal cleanup too.
Ingredients: 1 pound sirloin steak, about 1/2 inch thick
2 tablespoons grapeseed oil or canola oil
Instructions: Sprinkle steak with 1/4 teaspoon each salt and pepper. Heat a large cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat. Add the steak and cook until charred on one side, about 3 minutes. Turn the steak over and add oil, garlic, thyme, sage and rosemary. Cook, stirring the herbs occasionally, until an instant-read thermometer inserted in the thickest part of the steak reaches 125 degrees F for medium-rare, 3 to 4 minutes. Transfer the steak to a plate and top with the garlic and herbs. Tent with foil.

Add escarole and the remaining 1/4 teaspoon each salt and pepper to the pan. Cook, stirring often, until the escarole starts to wilt, about 2 minutes. Thinly slice the steak and serve with the escarole and crispy herbs.

https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/273194.Title: Tex-Mex Pasta Salad
https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/273194.Description: A light and creamy green-salsa dressing highlights this easy pasta salad with Southwestern flavors.
Ingredients: 0.75 cup frozen shelled edamame (4 oz.), cooked according to package directions, drained and cooled
0.5 cup cooked orzo, preferably whole-wheat, cooled
Instructions: Whisk salsa and yogurt in a small bowl. Set aside.

Combine tomatoes, bell pepper, edamame, orzo, onion, and cheese in a bowl. Add salt, pepper, and the salsa dressing; toss to combine. Season with hot sauce to taste, sprinkle with pepitas, and serve with lime wedge, if desired.

https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/270571.Title: Salmon Couscous Salad
https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/270571.Description: This healthy and easy salad is designed to be made with precooked or leftover salmon. To quickly cook salmon, lightly brush with olive oil, then roast in a 450 degrees F oven until the fish is opaque and firm, 8 to 12 minutes.
Ingredients: 0.25 cup cooked Israeli couscous, preferably whole-wheat
Instructions: Coat a small skillet with cooking spray and heat over medium-high heat. Add mushrooms and eggplant; cook, stirring, until lightly browned and juices have been released, 3 to 5 minutes. Remove from heat and set aside.
Toss spinach with 1 Tbsp. plus 1 tsp. vinaigrette and place on a 9-inch plate.
Toss couscous with the remaining 2 tsp. vinaigrette and place on top of the spinach. Place salmon on top. Top with the cooked vegetables, dried apricots, and goat cheese.

https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/269844.Title: Vegan Superfood Grain Bowls
https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/269844.Description: This nutrient-packed vegan recipe comes together in 15 minutes. Pack these ahead to keep on hand for easy meal-prep lunches or dinners.
Ingredients: 1 (8 ounce) package refrigerated cooked whole baby beets, sliced (or 2 cups from salad bar)
Instructions: Prepare quinoa according to package directions; set aside to cool.
Combine hummus and lemon juice in a small bowl. Thin with water to desired dressing consistency. Divide the dressing among 4 small condiment containers with lids and refrigerate.
Divide baby kale among 4 single-serving containers with lids. Top each with 1/2 cup of the quinoa, 1/2 cup beets, 1/4 cup edamame and 1 tablespoon sunflower seeds.
When ready to eat, top with 1/4 avocado and the hummus dressing.

https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/269496.Title: One-Pot Garlicky Shrimp & Spinach
https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/269496.Description: This shrimp and spinach recipe is a simple one-pot meal with a flavorful pan sauce. Make it tonight to simplify dinnertime and satisfy the family.
Ingredients: 1 pound shrimp (21-30 count), peeled and deveined
Instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add half the garlic and cook until beginning to brown, 1 to 2 minutes. Add 1 pound of spinach and ¼ teaspoon salt and toss to coat. Cook, stirring once or twice, until mostly wilted, 3 to 5 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in 1 tablespoon lemon juice. Transfer to a bowl and keep warm.

Increase heat to medium-high and add the remaining 2 tablespoons oil to the pot. Add the remaining garlic and cook until beginning to brown, 1 to 2 minutes. Add 1 pound shrimp, ¼ teaspoon crushed red pepper and the remaining ⅛ teaspoon salt; cook, stirring, until the shrimp are just cooked through, 3 to 5 minutes more. Serve the shrimp over the spinach, sprinkled with 1 tablespoon parsley and 1½ teaspoons lemon zest.

https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/260717.Title: Stuffed Sweet Potato with Hummus Dressing
https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/260717.Description: Hearty yet simple to prepare, this stuffed sweet potato with black beans, kale and hummus dressing is a fantastic 5-ingredient lunch for one!
Instructions: Prick sweet potato all over with a fork. Microwave on High until cooked through, 7 to 10 minutes.

Meanwhile, wash kale and drain, allowing water to cling to the leaves. Place in a medium saucepan; cover and cook over medium-high heat, stirring once or twice, until wilted. Add beans; add a tablespoon or two of water if the pot is dry. Continue cooking, uncovered, stirring occasionally, until the mixture is steaming hot, 1 to 2 minutes.

Split the sweet potato open and top with the kale and bean mixture. Combine hummus and 2 tablespoons water in a small dish. Add additional water as needed to reach desired consistency. Drizzle the hummus dressing over the stuffed sweet potato.

https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/265885.Title: No-Cook Black Bean Salad
https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/265885.Description: A classic black bean salad is a must for picnics and potlucks. This vegan version gets its creaminess from blended avocado. Any mix of salad greens will work well, but try arugula if you want to give this hearty salad a peppery kick.
Ingredients: 1 medium ripe avocado, pitted and roughly chopped
2 medium ears corn, kernels removed, or 2 cups frozen corn, thawed and patted dry
Instructions: Place onion in a medium bowl and cover with cold water. Set aside. Combine avocado, cilantro, lime juice, oil, garlic and salt in a mini food processor. Process, scraping down the sides as needed, until smooth and creamy.
Just before serving, combine salad greens, corn, tomatoes and beans in a large bowl. Drain the onions and add to the bowl, along with the avocado dressing. Toss to coat.

https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/269498.Title: Superfood Chopped Salad with Salmon & Creamy Garlic Dressing
https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/269498.Description: Curly kale forms the base of this salad, but you could use chard or spinach. To the greens, add a multitude of chopped veggies, such as broccoli, cabbage and carrots. Finish with rich salmon for protein and a drizzle of creamy yogurt dressing to bring it all together.
Ingredients: 2 teaspoons reduced-sodium tamari or soy sauce
Instructions: Arrange rack in upper third of oven. Preheat broiler to high. Line a baking sheet with foil.
Place salmon on the prepared baking sheet, skin-side down. Broil, rotating the pan from front to back once, until the salmon is opaque in the center, 8 to 12 minutes. Cut into 4 portions.
Meanwhile, whisk yogurt, mayonnaise, lemon juice, Parmesan, parsley, chives, tamari (or soy sauce), garlic and pepper in a small bowl.

Combine kale, broccoli, cabbage, carrots and sunflower seeds in a large bowl. Add 3/4 cup of the dressing and toss to coat. Divide the salad among 4 dinner plates and top each with a piece of salmon and about 1 tablespoon of the remaining dressing.

https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/275783.Title: Stuffed Potatoes with Salsa & Beans
https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/275783.Description: Taco night meets baked potato night with this simple recipe for loaded baked potatoes with salsa, beans and avocado. This easy, healthy family dinner comes together with just 10 minutes of active time, so you can make it on even the busiest of weeknights. This recipe is just as delicious with sweet potatoes in place of russets.
Ingredients: 1 (15 ounce) can pinto beans, rinsed, warmed and lightly mashed
Instructions: Pierce potatoes all over with a fork. Microwave on Medium, turning once or twice, until soft, about 20 minutes. (Alternatively, bake potatoes at 425 degrees F until tender, 45 minutes to 1 hour.) Transfer to a clean cutting board and let cool slightly.
Holding them with a kitchen towel to protect your hands, make a lengthwise cut to open the potato, but don't cut all the way through. Pinch the ends to expose the flesh.
Top each potato with some salsa, avocado, beans and jalapeños. Serve warm.

https://www.eatingwell.com/brussels-spro.Title: Brussels Sprouts, Kale & Pear Salad
https://www.eatingwell.com/brussels-spro.Description: This crisp and colorful salad celebrates the best of cool-weather produce, including Brussels sprouts, kale, pears and pomegranate seeds.
Ingredients: 2 small cloves garlic, grated (about ¼ teaspoon)
1 medium bunch kale, stemmed and chopped (about 10 cups)
10 ounces Brussels sprouts, trimmed and thinly sliced (about 4 cups)
Instructions: Whisk 4 tablespoons vinegar, 1½ tablespoons maple syrup, 2 teaspoons mustard, ½ teaspoon salt, ½ teaspoon pepper and the grated garlic together in a large bowl. While whisking, gradually add 5 tablespoons oil; whisk until emulsified.
Add chopped kale and sliced Brussels sprouts to the bowl. Massage the mixture with clean hands until the kale is bright green and reduced in volume by about half, about 1 minute.
Add pear slices, ½ cup pomegranate arils, the chopped walnuts and ¾ cup Parmesan; toss to combine. Top with the remaining ¼ cup Parmesan.

https://www.eatingwell.com/20-minute-chi.Title: 20-Minute Chickpea Soup
https://www.eatingwell.com/20-minute-chi.Description: When dinner needs to happen fast, turn to this creamy chickpea soup that's pulled together in just 20 minutes and features chickpeas and sweet potatoes.
Ingredients: 3 large cloves garlic, finely chopped (about 2 tablespoons)
2 small sweet potatoes, scrubbed and chopped (about 2 cups)
Instructions: Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a large saucepan over high heat. Add chopped onion, chopped garlic, 2 tablespoons taco seasoning and ⅛ teaspoon salt. Cook, stirring often, until fragrant and the onion starts to soften, 3 to 5 minutes.

Stir in 4 cups broth, the rinsed chickpeas, chopped sweet potatoes and diced tomatoes. Cover and bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce heat to maintain a lively simmer; cook, covered and stirring occasionally, until the sweet potatoes are tender, 8 to 10 minutes.
Stir in the softened cream cheese; return to a lively simmer. Stir in 5 ounces baby spinach; cook until wilted.
Divide the soup among 6 bowls. Garnish with cilantro and tortilla strips, if desired.

https://www.eatingwell.com/sheet-pan-sal.Title: Sheet-Pan Salmon with Bok Choy & Rice
https://www.eatingwell.com/sheet-pan-sal.Description: This five-ingredient dinner features tender salmon fillets that roast alongside crisp bok choy, all served over a bed of brown rice.
Ingredients: 2 tablespoons neutral oil, such as canola or avocado, divided
1 pound baby bok choy, sliced in half lengthwise
Instructions: Line a large rimmed baking sheet with foil and place on middle oven rack; preheat oven to 425°F.

Whisk 1 tablespoon oil, 2 tablespoons miso and 1 tablespoon soy sauce together in a small bowl. Arrange 4 salmon fillets, skin-side down, in the center of the preheated pan. Brush the salmon with half of the miso mixture, about 2 tablespoons. Set the remaining miso mixture aside.

Toss bok choy with the remaining 1 tablespoon oil and ¼ teaspoon salt in a large bowl and arrange, cut-side down, around the salmon. Roast until the bok choy stems are tender, about 8 to 10 minutes. Flip the bok choy; brush with the remaining miso mixture and return to the oven. Cook until the salmon flakes easily with a fork and the bok choy leaves are browned, about 5 minutes.
Divide 2 cups rice among 4 plates. Top with the salmon and bok choy.

https://www.eatingwell.com/chickpea-grai.Title: Chickpea Grain Bowl with Feta & Tomatoes
https://www.eatingwell.com/chickpea-grai.Description: This chickpea-farro grain bowl is a hearty dish that’s packed with plant-based protein, fiber and tons of fresh flavor.
Instructions: Whisk 2 tablespoons oil, 1 tablespoon lemon juice, 1 tablespoon vinegar, 1 teaspoon oregano, ¼ teaspoon pepper and ⅛ teaspoon salt together in a small bowl.
Place ¾ cup cooked farro in each of 4 bowls. Top each with ¼ cup chickpeas, ¼ cup tomatoes, ¼ cup cucumber, ¼ avocado, ¼ cup feta and 1 tablespoon dressing.

https://www.eatingwell.com/green-smoothi.Title: The Only Green Smoothie Recipe You’ll Ever Need
https://www.eatingwell.com/green-smoothi.Description: This vibrant green smoothie recipe with spinach, banana, mango and pineapple is a refreshing way to start your day.
Instructions: Combine 2 cups spinach, 1 cup almond milk, 1 banana, ½ cup frozen mango, ½ cup frozen pineapple and 1 tablespoon chia seeds in a blender; process until smooth, about 1 minute. Pour into a large glass and serve immediately.

https://www.eatingwell.com/peanut-butter.Title: Peanut Butter-Banana Flaxseed Smoothie
https://www.eatingwell.com/peanut-butter.Description: This peanut butter-banana flaxseed smoothie is a creamy, satisfying drink that’s perfect for breakfast.
Ingredients: 2 frozen sliced very ripe medium bananas (about 1¼ cups)
¼ cup whole-milk plain strained (Greek-style) yogurt
¼ cup smooth natural peanut butter
1 tablespoon ground flaxseed, plus more for garnish
Instructions: Combine frozen sliced bananas, ½ cup almond milk, ¼ cup yogurt, ¼ cup peanut butter, 1 tablespoon flaxseed, 1 tablespoon maple syrup (if using), ½ teaspoon vanilla, ⅛ teaspoon cinnamon and a pinch of salt in a blender; process until smooth, about 1 minute.
Pour into 2 glasses. Garnish with additional ground flaxseed, if desired.

https://www.eatingwell.com/caprese-chick.Title: High-Protein Caprese Chickpea Salad
https://www.eatingwell.com/caprese-chick.Description: This fresh caprese chickpea salad is a fresh, protein- and fiber-packed, plant-based twist on the classic Italian favorite.
Ingredients: 1 small clove garlic, grated (about ½ teaspoon)
2 medium Persian cucumbers, thinly sliced (1¼ cups)
¼ cup thinly sliced fresh basil
Instructions: Whisk 3 tablespoons vinegar, 2 tablespoons oil, 2 teaspoons mustard, the grated garlic, ¼ teaspoon salt and ¼ teaspoon pepper together in a large bowl. Add rinsed chickpeas, halved tomatoes, sliced cucumbers, 1 cup mozzarella and ¼ cup basil; toss to coat. Refrigerate until ready to serve.

https://www.eatingwell.com/mango-lassi-s.Title: No-Added-Sugar Mango Lassi Smoothie
https://www.eatingwell.com/mango-lassi-s.Description: This high-protein mango lassi smoothie is the perfect fuel for your busy day! It features frozen mangoes, creamy Greek-style yogurt and hemp seeds.
Ingredients: ¼ cup whole-milk  plain strained (Greek-style) yogurt
Instructions: Place 1 date, 1 cup milk, ¼ cup yogurt, 1 cup frozen mango, ¼ teaspoon cardamom and 1 tablespoon hemp seeds in a blender. Process until smooth, about 1 minute, stopping to scrape down sides as needed.
Pour the smoothie into a glass; top with the remaining ½ tablespoon hemp seeds.

https://www.eatingwell.com/anti-inflamma.Title: Anti-Inflammatory Strawberry & Kale Salad with Burrata
https://www.eatingwell.com/anti-inflamma.Description: This strawberry-and-kale salad with burrata is a delicious, nutrient-packed dish that offers a host of anti-inflammatory benefits.
Ingredients: ¼ teaspoon coarsely ground black pepper, plus more for garnish
1 pound lacinato kale, stemmed and chopped (about 8 cups)
½ cup thinly sliced red onion
1 (4-ounce) ball burrata cheese, torn into ½-inch pieces
Instructions: Chop about 3 strawberries to equal ⅓ cup. Quarter the remaining strawberries and set aside. Process the chopped strawberries, 3 tablespoons vinegar, 1 tablespoon honey, ½ teaspoon salt and ¼ teaspoon pepper in a mini food processor until smooth, about 30 seconds. Add ¼ cup oil and pulse until combined, about 5 pulses.

Place chopped kale and ½ cup onion in a large bowl; drizzle with the dressing. Using clean hands, massage the mixture until the kale is well coated and slightly tender, about 2 minutes. Add the reserved quartered strawberries; toss to combine. Transfer to a large serving dish. Top with burrata pieces and sprinkle with ¼ cup walnuts. Garnish with additional pepper, if desired.

https://www.eatingwell.com/one-skillet-g.Title: One-Skillet Garlicky Salmon & Broccoli
https://www.eatingwell.com/one-skillet-g.Description: This one-skillet salmon and broccoli recipe is the perfect 20-minute dinner for busy weeknights.
Ingredients: 1¼ pounds skinless center-cut salmon fillet, cut into 1-inch pieces
2 red bell peppers, seeded and chopped (2 cups)
Instructions: Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a large nonstick skillet with a lid over medium-high heat. Add salmon pieces and half of the sliced garlic in an even layer. Sprinkle with ½ teaspoon each salt and crushed red pepper. Cook, uncovered, stirring and turning occasionally, until the salmon is opaque on all sides and just cooked through, 4 to 5 minutes. Using a fish spatula or tongs, transfer the salmon to a plate.

Without wiping the skillet clean, add 5 cups broccoli, the chopped bell peppers, 1 tablespoon water and the remaining sliced garlic and ¼ teaspoon salt. Cover and cook, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are tender-crisp, 4 to 5 minutes. Stir in 1½ tablespoons orange juice and 1 tablespoon tamari. Gently fold in the cooked salmon. Divide among 4 shallow bowls; spoon any remaining liquid from the pan over the bowls. Sprinkle with 1 teaspoon orange zest and 1 tablespoon scallions. Recipe developed by Marianne Williams

https://www.eatingwell.com/chickpea-beet.Title: No-Cook Chickpea, Beet & Quinoa Salad
https://www.eatingwell.com/chickpea-beet.Description: This easy no-cook chickpea salad comes together in minutes. With a bright lemony-garlic dressing, this salad is the perfect side to accompany grilled chicken or roasted salmon.
Ingredients: 1 cup coarsely chopped arugula or romaine lettuce
Instructions: Whisk 3 tablespoons oil, 2½ tablespoons lemon juice, garlic, 1 teaspoon Italian seasoning, ½ teaspoon salt and ¼ teaspoon pepper together in a large bowl. Add 2 cups beets, rinsed chickpeas, 1½ cups quinoa, 1 cup arugula (or romaine), diced celery and sliced scallions; toss to coat.

https://www.eatingwell.com/blueberry-pea.Title: Blueberry-Peach Chia Seed Smoothie
https://www.eatingwell.com/blueberry-pea.Description: This fruit smoothie is a nutrient-packed drink that blends frozen peaches and sweet frozen blueberries with a splash of almond milk and yogurt.
Ingredients: ½ cup whole-milk plain strained (Greek-style) yogurt
⅓ cup chopped pitted Medjool dates
¼ teaspoon ground cardamom or ground ginger
Instructions: Combine 2 cups almond milk, ½ cup yogurt, ⅓ cup dates, ¼ cup orange juice, 1¾ cups peaches, ¾ cup blueberries, 2 tablespoons chia seeds, 1 teaspoon vanilla, ¼ teaspoon cardamom (or ginger) and ⅛ teaspoon salt in a blender; process until smooth, about 1 minute. Divide between 2 glasses; serve immediately.

https://www.eatingwell.com/arugula-beet-.Title: Arugula, Beet & Feta Salad
https://www.eatingwell.com/arugula-beet-.Description: Peppery arugula and tender, sweet beets are balanced by a simple vinaigrette and briny bits of feta cheese in this salad.
Ingredients: ¼ teaspoon ground pepper, plus more for garnish
1 (8.8-ounce) package refrigerated cooked beets, such as Love Beets
Instructions: Stir sliced shallot, 3 tablespoons oil, 2 tablespoons vinegar, 2 teaspoons honey, ¼ teaspoon pepper and ⅛ teaspoon salt together in a large bowl until combined.
Drain beets and cut into 1-inch wedges; add to the dressing and toss to coat. Add arugula; toss gently to coat. Top with ½ cup feta and garnish with additional pepper, if desired.

https://www.eatingwell.com/tuna-chickpea.Title: High-Protein Tuna & Chickpea Salad Sandwich
https://www.eatingwell.com/tuna-chickpea.Description: This zesty tuna sandwich gets an extra boost of protein from chickpeas. Smashing some of the chickpeas into the tuna enhances the texture and helps hold the filling together.
Ingredients: 2 (5-ounce) cans solid white tuna in water, drained
Instructions: Whisk mayonnaise, chives, Sriracha, garlic, lemon juice, salt and pepper together in a small bowl.

Place chickpeas in a medium bowl. Using a fork, press and roughly smash some of the chickpeas (it’s OK if some remain whole). Add tuna to the chickpeas; stir to combine, using the fork to flake the tuna. Add the mayonnaise mixture and onion; stir until well combined.
Spread the mixture evenly over 4 bread slices (about 1/2 cup each). Top each with 1 lettuce leaf and top with the remaining bread slices. Recipe developed by Catherine Jessee

https://www.eatingwell.com/white-bean-sa.Title: High-Protein White Bean Salad with Feta & Lemon-Garlic Vinaigrette
https://www.eatingwell.com/white-bean-sa.Description: This no-cook white bean salad with feta and lemon-garlic vinaigrette is quick, protein-rich and perfect for lunch.
Ingredients: 1 small clove garlic, grated (about ¼ teaspoon)
¼ teaspoon coarsely ground black pepper
2 (15-ounce) cans no-salt-added cannellini beans, rinsed (about 3 cups)
Instructions: Whisk 2 tablespoons lemon juice, 2 tablespoons yogurt, ½ teaspoon mustard, the grated garlic, ¼ teaspoon pepper and ¼ teaspoon salt together in a large bowl. While whisking constantly, slowly stream in ¼ cup oil until combined. Add rinsed beans, 3 cups spinach, halved tomatoes, sliced shallots and 3 tablespoons dill; gently toss until evenly coated. Sprinkle with ½ cup feta and ¼ cup walnuts.

https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/807360.Title: Anti-Inflammatory Beet & Avocado Wrap
https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/807360.Description: This healthy wrap is packed with avocado and beets, two foods that can help fight inflammation. The tahini-lemon mixture adds brightness to this easy wrap.
Instructions: Whisk lemon juice, tahini, oil, salt and pepper together in a medium bowl. Add beets; toss to coat.
Spread hummus evenly over 1 side of tortilla. Place lettuce over hummus; top with beet mixture and avocado slices. Roll up burrito-style; slice in half.

https://www.eatingwell.com/avocado-chick.Title: 5-Ingredient Avocado & Chickpea Salad
https://www.eatingwell.com/avocado-chick.Description: This avocado and chickpea salad is a fresh, flavorful dish that comes together in minutes. Creamy avocado pairs perfectly with hearty chickpeas for a filling, plant-based meal.
Instructions: Whisk 4 tablespoons lemon juice, 2 tablespoons oil, ¼ teaspoon salt and ¼ teaspoon pepper in a large bowl. Add rinsed chickpeas, halved tomatoes, sliced onion and diced avocado; toss gently to coat.

https://www.eatingwell.com/raspberry-pea.Title: Raspberry-Peach Chia Seed Smoothie
https://www.eatingwell.com/raspberry-pea.Description: This creamy raspberry-peach chia seed smoothie is the best way to start your day. Or to recharge in the afternoon.
Ingredients: ½ cup whole-milk plain strained (Greek-style) yogurt
Instructions: Place 1½ cups soy milk, ½ cup yogurt, ¼ cup chia seeds, 4 dates, 1½ cups raspberries, 1 cup peaches and ⅛ teaspoon salt in a blender. Process until smooth, stirring occasionally to help blend if needed, about 1 minute. Pour into 2 glasses. This recipe was developed by Marianne Williams

https://www.eatingwell.com/cucumber-blue.Title: Cucumber-Blueberry Spinach Salad
https://www.eatingwell.com/cucumber-blue.Description: This spinach-blueberry salad has the perfect balance of sweet and tart flavors, complemented by refreshing cucumber slices and creamy goat cheese.
Ingredients: 1/4 cup plus 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil
1 cup thinly sliced unpeeled English cucumber
Instructions: Combine 3/4 cup blueberries, vinegar, honey and salt in a food processor; process until fully combined, about 15 seconds. With the processor running, slowly pour oil through the chute until the dressing is emulsified, about 30 seconds.
Place spinach, cucumber and the remaining 1/2 cup blueberries in a large bowl. Drizzle with the dressing; toss until well coated. Transfer to a serving dish; top with goat cheese and almonds.

https://www.eatingwell.com/italian-love-.Title: Mom’s Italian Love Cake
https://www.eatingwell.com/italian-love-.Description: Italian Love Cake is a layered dessert that uses simple ingredients and features layers of cake, ricotta cheese and chocolate pudding.
Ingredients: 1 (13.25-ounce) box devil’s food chocolate cake mix
Instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Coat a 9-by-13-inch baking pan with cooking spray.

Place 2 containers ricotta, 1 cup sugar and 1 teaspoon vanilla in a large bowl; mix with an electric mixer on medium speed until combined. Add 4 eggs, one at a time, mixing to incorporate after each addition until combined.

In a separate large bowl, combine cake mix, 1 cup water, ½ cup oil and the remaining 3 eggs; whisk until smooth. Pour the cake batter into the prepared pan and spread into an even layer. Pour the ricotta mixture on top of the batter in an even layer, completely covering the batter.
Bake until the cake is cooked through (it should slightly jiggle, but not be liquidy), about 1 hour. Transfer the pan to a wire rack and let the cake cool to room temperature, about 3 hours.

Meanwhile, combine chocolate pudding mix and 2 cups milk in a large bowl; mix until fully combined. Let stand for 2 minutes. Fold in 1 container whipped topping until fully incorporated. Set aside until ready to frost the cake.
Once the cake is cool, spread the chocolate pudding mixture on top of the cake. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours (and up to overnight).

https://www.eatingwell.com/black-bean-br.Title: High-Fiber Black Bean Brownies
https://www.eatingwell.com/black-bean-br.Description: These black bean brownies are everything you could possibly want—moist, rich and fudgy with big chocolate flavor.
Instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Coat a 9-inch-square baking pan with cooking spray.
Place rinsed beans in a food processor; process until a mostly smooth, thick paste forms, about 1 minute, stopping to scrape down the sides as needed.

Add 3 large eggs, ¼ cup oil, 2 tablespoons maple syrup and 1 tablespoon vanilla; pulse until combined, about 5 pulses. Add ½ cup sugar, ¼ cup cocoa and ½ teaspoon each baking powder, coffee granules and salt; pulse until thoroughly combined, about 5 pulses.
Transfer the batter to the prepared pan, spreading into an even layer. Sprinkle ½ cup chocolate chips over the top.

Bake until the center is fully set and the edges just begin pulling away from the pan’s sides, 23 to 25 minutes. Let cool in the pan on a wire rack until room temperature, about 30 minutes, before cutting and serving.

https://www.eatingwell.com/banana-cake-w.Title: Banana Cake with Cream Cheese Frosting
https://www.eatingwell.com/banana-cake-w.Description: This banana cake with cream cheese frosting is a warmly spiced dessert for fall gatherings, afternoon coffee breaks or anytime you have overripe bananas on hand.
Ingredients: ⅔ cup packed light brown sugar
1 teaspoon ground cinnamon, plus more for sprinkling
1 teaspoon ground ginger, plus more for sprinkling
½ teaspoon ground cardamom, plus more for sprinkling
6 ounces cream cheese (about ¾ cup), softened
Instructions: Prepare cake: Preheat oven to 350°F. Coat an 8-inch square baking pan with cooking spray.

Combine mashed bananas, ⅔ cup brown sugar, 2 eggs, the melted butter, 1 teaspoon cinnamon, 1 teaspoon ginger, ½ teaspoon cardamom and 1 teaspoon vanilla in a large bowl; whisk well until combined.
